# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 22)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of the first year; now nearly three weeks into the new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Quallingham)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; threatening rain (persistent but held off); frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett ("Old Ilrine"), herbalist born at Quenwick; Eldette Corrett, cooper born at Gulton; Thidrek Corrett, smith; Ridan Corrett, glazier born at Coldcombe; Jotho Corrett ("Jotho the Younger"); Aessa Hollwood, ferryman born in Salwick; Cotho Hollwood, mason; Halan Hollwood, shepherd

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- **Admiration for Caleb Garth**: Strong admiration for his work knowledge; Caleb greatly admires her
- **Business Philosophy**: Hopes to improve great piece of land and build many good cottages
- **Final Grange Encounter with Will**: Will declared passionately that best is over with him; acknowledged he would never woo her; spoke plainly that he would live like one who had seen heaven in a trance
- **Misinterpretation**: Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced sickening certainty that Will meant his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- **Internal Resolution**: Though thought throbbed through her that she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to simple friendship and cruel obstruction from husband's injurious act
- **Departure and Longing**: Caught sight of Will with portfolio on road; passed him as he raised his hat; felt pang at being seated in exaltation while leaving him behind; wished she had known before so they could be happy thinking of each other though forever parted
- **About Casaubon's Codicil**: Forced to keep money that ought to have been his under Casaubon's codicil, causing her distress

**Will Ladislaw**
- **Grange Declaration**: Spoke impetuously about what he cares for most being forbidden him by his own pride and honor
- **Emotional State at Grange**: Consciousness overflowed by something suppressing utterance upon seeing her; passionate love for her which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- **After Parting**: As carriage grew smaller, his certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- **Remaining at Middlemarch**: Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting from Dorothea; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond Lydgate
- **Scandal**: Mrs. Cadwallader reports scandal spreading about Will making scandal by warbling continually with Lydgate's wife
- **Raffles' Secret**: Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this, treating as card to play
- **Previous Family Revelations**: Father was at Boulogne, very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- **Bulstrode's Offer (Rejected)**: **Will rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth are important; recognized stain he cannot help through his mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; states it ought to lie with a man's self that he is a gentleman; departed with determined quickness**
- **Morning After Rejection**: Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court; peculiar man lacking curiosity about personal affairs; very fond of music
- **Working with Railroads**: Had business at Yoddrell's farm to measure and value outlying piece of land belonging to Lowick Manor; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents
- **Commitment to Fred Vincy**: Decided to take Fred on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Character**: Ruled absolutely only on other people's behalf; on ninety-nine points Mrs. Garth decided, but on hundredth point Caleb was immovable ruler

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother; intelligent, composed
- **Definitive Statement on Fred**: Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- **Reaction to Fred's News**: Upon Fred telling her of his engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Mr. Farebrother's delicate feeling
- **Internal Conflict and Resolution**: Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- **Present Activity**: Telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage; tells Rumpelstiltskin tale

**Fred Vincy**
- Son of Mr. Vincy; age four-and-twenty
- **Current Situation**: Rejected Church vocation; has taken his degree; encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm
- **Caleb's Offer Accepted**: Accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Disclosure to Father**: Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- **Casual Mention of Ladislaw News**: Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he had heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- **Acknowledged Debt**: Has acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged
- **Present Activity**: Seated near Mary at Lowick Parsonage during storytelling; watching her with admiration

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician in Middlemarch; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture; bought purple amethysts costing thirty pounds as bridal present for Rosamond; year's bills coming in; needs nothing less than thousand pounds to be freed from actual embarrassment
- **Conversation with Rosamond about Debt**: Had been preparing to discuss debt with Rosamond; she would not turn eyes on paper; quietly went out of room; seemed Rosamond had not identified herself with him as if creatures of different species
- **New Proposal to Rosamond - House Solution**: **Proposed they reduce expenses; suggested smaller house at thirty pounds per year instead of current ninety-pound house; noted Ned Plymdale and Miss Sophy Toller (soon to marry) would be glad to take their house with most of furniture; proposed employing Trumbull to speak to Plymdale**
- **Rosamond's Response to House Proposal**: **Left husband's knee and walked slowly to other end of room; tears came; immediately blamed him: "If we are to be in that position it will be entirely your own doing, Tertius"; claimed he will not behave as he ought to do to his own family; said Sir Godwin was very kind to her at Quallingham and would help if Lydgate showed proper regard; immediately walked out of room in silence with intense determination to hinder what Lydgate liked to do**
- **Rosamond's Interference**: **Returned home by Mr. Borthrop Trumbull's office; first time in her life Rosamond had thought of doing anything in business; felt equal to occasion; called on Trumbull at his office, asking whether Lydgate had called that morning to speak about disposing of their house; revoked his order to Borthrop Trumbull before New Year's Day party**
- **Emotional and Mental State**: Native warm-heartedness takes great deal of quenching; feels keenly manliness requires husband to feel that inexperienced girl got into trouble by marrying him; realizes Rosamond does not reverence his mind as he imagined; memory of Dorothea's voice—that voice of deep-souled womanhood—had remained within him as enkindling conceptions; now prey to worst irritation from second consciousness of wasted energy and degrading preoccupation; bitter incessant murmur: "This is what I am thinking of; and that is what I might have been thinking of"
- **Knowledge of Will-Dorothea Situation**: Knows a great deal more than he tells; imagines passionate attachment on both sides; understood the vacillation keeping Will at Middlemarch
- **Hospital Work**: Giving great deal of time to New Hospital; preparing new ward in case cholera comes
- **Encounter with Farebrother and Offer of Help**: Mr. Farebrother met Lydgate at Lowick Parsonage drawing-room; stepped out of whist-table to speak with him; offered friendly ear if Lydgate wanted to open himself about any difficulty
- **Lydgate's Response to Offer**: Could not bear the offer of help; feared mention of his case would imply wanting specific things; at that moment suicide seemed easier
- **Temporary Comfort on New Year's Eve**: Evening of party, Lydgate observed Rosamond was more lively than usual and seemed interested in pleasing him; began to search for account of experiments; felt again some old delightful absorption; Rosamond played quiet music which was as helpful to his meditation as plash of oar on evening lake
- **Interruption and Shock**: **As Lydgate was absorbed in construction of new controlling experiment, Rosamond, leaving piano and leaning back in her chair, revealed she had revoked his order to Trumbull; Lydgate felt bitter disappointment as if he had opened door out of suffocating place and found it walled up**
- **Morning After New Year's Day Party Confrontation**: **Had to learn that Rosamond had revoked his order to Borthrop Trumbull; at breakfast said he would try to see Trumbull to advertise house in 'Pioneer' and 'Trumpet'; Rosamond stared at him in mute amazement; only half an hour before Lydgate had been fastening up her plaits and talking "little language" of affection; shock he received was confused pain; laid down knife and fork and threw himself back in chair with cool irony in his tone**
- **New Confrontation**: **When Rosamond defended her interference by claiming to protect him from degrading step and himself from poor opinion of others, Lydgate responded with anger at her contradicting his orders secretly; Rosamond said his violent speech about necessity did not alter her opinion; he should try every other means rather than take step so painful to her; advertising house would be degrading**
- **Paralyzed by Opposing Impulses**: **Sat paralyzed: wanted to smash object to produce impression or tell her brutally he was master and she must obey; dreaded effect on their mutual life; had growing dread of Rosamond's quiet elusive obstinacy, which would not allow any assertion of power to be final; she had touched him in spot of keenest feeling by implying she had been deluded with false vision of happiness in marrying him; realization he was not master; his resolution beginning to relax under her torpedo contact; swallowed half his cup of coffee and rose to go**
- **Attempted Compromise**: **Rosamond requested he not go to Trumbull at present—until it has been seen that there are no other means; asked promise not to go to him for few weeks or without telling her; she felt safer not betraying that she had written to Sir Godwin**
- **New Year's Day Dinner at Her Father's**: **Looking mildly neutral toward him in remembrance of his ill-tempered behavior at breakfast; he carrying much deeper effect from inward conflict; his flushed effort while talking to Mr. Farebrother was symptom of wavering resolve and benumbed response to old stimuli of enthusiasm**
- **Plans for Quallingham**: **Never mentioned to Rosamond his brooding purpose of going to Quallingham; did not want to admit what would appear to her a concession to her wishes after indignant refusal; really expecting to set off soon; a slice of the railway would enable him to manage whole journey and back in four days**
- **Nearly Three Weeks into New Year**: **In total ignorance of Rosamond's expectations, seeing bills come in, feeling that Dover's use of his advantage over other creditors was imminent**
- **Letter from Sir Godwin**: **Received letter from Sir Godwin Lydgate (delayed nearly three weeks); Sir Godwin refused aid of any kind, stating wife should not write to him on business matters; stated he cannot supply thousand pounds or half that sum; his own family drains him to the last penny with two younger sons and three daughters; criticized Lydgate for getting through his own money quickly and making a mess; suggested he should go somewhere else; stated he had nothing to do with men of his profession; could not help; did best as guardian letting him have his own way in medicine; noted he might have gone into army or Church where money would have held out; uncle Charles had grudge against him for not going into his profession but not Sir Godwin; always wished him well but must consider himself on his own legs entirely now**
- **Reaction to Sir Godwin's Letter**: **Upon reading, said he had nearly resolved on going to Quallingham—would have cost him pain but might have been use; now no use thinking of anything; accused Rosamond of always counteracting him secretly; said she deluded him with false assent and then he was at mercy of her devices; told her if she means to resist every wish he expresses, say so and defy him, so he shall at least know what he is doing**

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Aware that Lydgate is proud man; had been playing whist to satisfy his mother
- **Awareness of Lydgate's Situation**: After conversation at Mr. Toller's, learned something which made him watch eagerly for opportunity
- **At Lowick Parsonage**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate; disclosed that Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money
- **Present Activity**: Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; fond of horseback riding; victorious obstinacy which never wastes energy
- **Riding Incident and Accident**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of her baby
- **Current State**: Regaining brilliant health; now possessing knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Disclosure and House Proposal**: **When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with pretty congratulations about coming marriage instead; had already secretly disobeyed him by asking her father to help them; her father said, "I am more likely to want help myself"**
- **Business Intervention**: **First time in her life thought of doing anything in form of business; felt equal to occasion; intense dislike turned her quiet tenacity into active invention; called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; Trumbull received her with finest manners, stirred by certainty that Lydgate was in difficulties; asked Trumbull whether Lydgate had called that morning to speak about disposing of their house; revoked Lydgate's order to Trumbull before New Year's Day party**
- **Written to Sir Godwin**: **Had written to Sir Godwin Lydgate with winning appeal requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks, every day disappointed; felt safer not betraying this in conversation with Lydgate**
- **Reaction to Sir Godwin's Refusal Letter**: **When letter arrived addressed to Lydgate from Sir Godwin, was full of hope; perhaps particular note to her enclosed; fact he was written to seemed to certify answer was thoroughly compliant; too much excited by these thoughts to do anything but light stitching in warm corner of dining-room with outside of momentous letter before her; about twelve heard husband's step in passage, tripping to open door, said in lightest tones, "Tertius, come in here—here is a letter for you"**
- **After Receiving Refusal**: **When Rosamond finished reading Sir Godwin's refusal letter, sat quite still with hands folded before her, restraining any show of keen disappointment, entrenching herself in quiet passivity under husband's wrath**

**Mr. Borthrop Trumbull**
- Auctioneer and man of business; received Rosamond with finest manners at his office
- **Sensibility and Benevolence**: Much sensibility to Rosamond's charms; good-natured fibre stirred by certainty that Lydgate was in difficulties; felt young lady with highest personal attractions likely to feel pinch of trouble; stood before her trimming and comporting himself with eager solicitude, chiefly benevolent

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Major Development**: Approximately fifteen months after Peter Featherstone's death, became proprietor of Stone Court through Joshua Rigg's land sale
- **Raffles' Appearances**: Met Mr. Raffles unexpectedly at Stone Court; Raffles recognized Bulstrode after twenty-five years; offered him quarterly annuity payments; Raffles demanded two hundred pounds to leave immediately, refused regular annuity, departed by three o'clock coach; later appeared wanting cool five-and-twenty pounds to go away; declared would come back before long
- **Bulstrode's Terror**: Feels helpless; certain that Raffles—unless providence sent death—would come back
- **Past Life**: Young banker's clerk with agreeable person; eminent though young member of Calvinistic dissenting church; **happiest time was spiritual conviction and sense of pardon; that was spot he would choose now to awake in and find rest a dream**
- **Dunkirk Connection**: Became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business; one source of magnificent profit was easy reception of any goods offered without strict inquiry as to where they came from
- **Moral Compromise**: Remembered first moments of shrinking filled with private arguments taking form of prayer; justified business through theological reasoning; perpetual self-justification; soul saturated with belief he did everything for God's sake, indifferent to it for his own; yet if could be back in youthful poverty, would choose to be missionary
- **Later Years**: After five years wife died; gradually withdrew capital but did not make sacrifices to end business, which was carried on for thirteen years before collapsing; became banker, Churchman, public benefactor
- **Current Crisis**: When respectability had lasted nearly thirty years, that past had risen and immersed his thought
- **Nature of His Hypocrisy**: Not coarse hypocrite consciously affecting beliefs; simply man whose desires had been stronger than theoretic beliefs, who gradually explained gratification of desires into satisfactory agreement with beliefs
- **Repentance and Restitution**: Had long poured out utterances of repentance; threatening Providence urged him to kind of propitiation which was not simply doctrinal transaction
- **Offer to Will and Reaction**: Wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; Will asked if Bulstrode had been connected with pawnbroker's business where stolen goods received; Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain of his ground; could not tell lie; answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at his death; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept like woman—first time encountered open expression of scorn from any man higher than Raffles

**Mr. Raffles**
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claims to be visiting stepson Joshua Rigg
- **Critical Discovery and Secret**: Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; **deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode**—holds secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as card to play
